children: Australian wages grew at their fastest pace in nearly three years in the September quarter, adding to signs the labour market remains tight and validating the aggressive rate rises this year to rein in inflation.

Figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed on Wednesday its wage price index rose 1.1% in the September quarter, the highest since the December quarter 2023. That followed five straight quarters of growth of around 0.8% and exceeded analysts' forecasts for a 0.9% rise.
Annual pay growth picked up to 3.5%, from 3.2% the previous quarter, as the private sector and public sector recorded strong rises in wages at 3.4% and 3.9%, respectively.

The ABS noted that wage setting decisions from the Fair Work Commission to lift minimal wages by 4.75% from July were a key driver of private sector wages, and pay rises for state government front-line workers contributed to the rise in public sector wages.
"Australia is in the uncommon position of having unemployment, interest rates and wages all rising at the same time," said Harry McAuley, an economist for Oxford Economics Australia.
"While we don't see further rate hikes in the immediate future, we do expect the unemployment rate and wage growth to remain elevated through 2027."
The Reserve Bank of Australia has judged the labour market to be a little tight, one reason it raised interest rates a fifth time in November to an 18-year high of 4.85% to fight sticky inflation.

There are, however, signs that the labour market is weakening, with the unemployment rate hitting a five-year high of 4.7% in September. Those concerns led three board members to oppose a rate rise earlier this month, worried the economy might be approaching a "materially sharper downturn".

Australia's oldest retailer David Jones will slash 1,500 jobs by the year-end. Home improvement retailer Bunnings said on Tuesday it would cut around 230 permanent roles, adding to anecdotal evidence of a broader rise in layoffs.
That raised the stakes for jobs data due on Thursday where forecasts are centred on a rise of 25,000 jobs in October and a steady unemployment rate at 4.7%.

Markets largely shrugged off the data, given it is backward-looking. Swaps still imply a 75% probability that interest rates have peaked in Australia, with about 20 basis points of policy easing to come by the end of 2027. (0#AUDIRPR)
